main_defect: The response treats the Clear formatting task as blocked and asks the user three questions instead of formatting the attached list (or applying the IEEE template); the expected signals explicitly say the response should contain no questions, so the questions-for-input approach is the core defect, though each question does state its use.

R1.evidence: Every action ends with a domain tag ("Deterministic, Clear domain.") but no action gives a one-line reason for the domain choice.

R2.evidence: The expected domain is Clear and the response marks all three actions "Clear domain", matching the prompt's expected classification.

R3.evidence: Each action is a single step as Clear requires ("Paste the plain text list...", "Tell me whether entries are books...", "Tell me if you want citations numbered...").

R4.evidence: All actions are Clear and ordered by blocker size: the missing-input blocker comes first ("This removes the missing-input blocker"), then template and ordering blockers. No Chaotic/Confused/Complex items to sequence.

R5.evidence: Each deterministic action carries a Gherkin test, e.g. "Given a line with author, title, publisher, year, When I format it, Then the entry matches IEEE book form."

R6.evidence: R6 does not apply to this prompt (no likely-wrong-answer line).

R7.evidence: Three questions with stated use ("I will format each entry as a numbered IEEE reference", etc.), which fits the letter of Section 2, but the prompt states the list is attached and the expected signals say no questions; the material should contain the answers, so asking was not justified.

R8.evidence: No uncalibrated hedges found (check report banned_total 0); no material uncertainty in the recommendation requires a probability or IPCC term.

R9.evidence: Headline first, End begins "I recommend that we", Self-test last with all required block lines, 3 actions each with increment, blocker, test, and domain. Check report: zero banned words, zero dashes, no overlong sentences, passive use minimal. The one citation [1] has a matching References entry tagged [P]; the script's "citation with no reference" flag appears to be a parse artifact since the entry is present.
